terms.meaning: a plain text format where symbols such as hash marks create headings and bold text
a link written in double square brackets that points to another note by its title
a function passed in by a parent that the child calls to report a change

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in React, icons, the Note type and the voice button. This section only sets up the file.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond normal file setup.

sections.name: NoteEditorProps
sections.title: Inputs the editor receives
sections.what: Defines what the editor needs: the note itself, a function to save changes, and a function to delete the note.
sections.why: Likely reason: the editor does not store changes itself. It reports them upward so the parent decides how to save.
sections.watch_out: Field names passed to the update function must match the note's fields, or the change will not be saved as expected.

sections.name: NoteEditor (part 1)
sections.title: Wiki link helper, title and voice input
sections.what: Defines a helper that would turn double-bracket links into highlighted text, though nothing here calls it. Shows the editable title and a voice button that appends a timestamped transcript to the body, plus a delete button.
sections.why: Likely reason: the helper was meant for showing the body with links styled. Reason for it being unused is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The transcript is added to the body as it was when recording started, so text typed during a recording can be overwritten.

sections.name: NoteEditor (part 2)
sections.title: Tags, body text and last-changed time
sections.what: Shows tags as a comma-separated text box, the large body text area, and when the note was last changed. Tags are split on commas, trimmed, and empty ones removed before saving.
sections.why: Likely reason: storing tags as a list while showing a simple line of text is easier to type.
sections.watch_out: The tag box is rebuilt from the saved list on every change, so a comma typed at the end disappears straight away.

summary: The editing panel for one note: title, tags, a large Markdown text box, a voice dictation button, and delete.
purpose: Lets the user write and tidy one note at a time.
why: Likely reason: keeps note editing in its own part, so the Notes page only has to choose which note is open.
how: Shows the title, tags and body of the note it receives. Each change is passed back to the parent straight away. The voice button adds a timestamped transcript at the end of the body. Delete asks the parent to remove the note. A helper can turn double-bracket links into highlighted text, but nothing calls it in this file.
inputs: One note with its title, tags, body and last-changed time, plus two functions from the parent: one to update and one to delete.
outputs: Update and delete requests to the parent, and the on-screen editor.
risks: The helper for highlighting wiki links is defined but never called, so links are not styled. Changes are sent upward on every keystroke. Typing a comma at the end of the tags box removes it straight away, which makes adding a second tag awkward.
debug: If a title or tag does not save, check the update function that NotesView passes in. If the voice text is missing, check the VoiceRecorderButton and the transcribe endpoint. If the time shown is wrong, check the note's updated time.
